newsitem.title: FRANCE: French beet conditions good despite pest pressure.
newsitem.headline: French beet conditions good despite pest pressure.

text.p: Recent rain helped French sugar beets make swift progress but warm and wet conditions in May increased pest pressure on the crop, planters said on Thursday.
"Pest pressure is strong in all regions but under control with no significant damage reported," planters said in their latest crop survey up to May 20.
Marginal pest damage was reported in the Aisne, the Somme, the North, Oise and Calvados region, they said.
The survey also showed that beet development was now in line with an average year though growth conditions greatly vary between regions.

As previously reported farmers were able to complete their sowings eight days ahead of an average year. Dry conditions up until April 25 slowed down beet growth but recent rains helped make up for that delay.
"As of May 20 drought-induced delays in development have been made up. Vegetation development is in line with an average year," the survey said.

Last year vegetation development was six days behind an average year. On 64 percent of the fields, beets have now reached for the four leaves development stage against 56 percent at same time last year.
Frost and drought damage will force farmers to redrill only a marginal 0.5 percent of total area sown.
Planters also said there were less fields with a low number of beets of hectare than last year.
Overall (beet) population levels are satisfactory even if there may be some damage due to thunderstorms, the survey showed.
Rain since April 25 was expected to help reduce the water supply shortfall resulting from nearly four months of drought, they said.
Between May 1 and 20 cumulative rainfall was 66 mm, above the average 64 mm for the whole month.
Between December and April the cumulative rainfall for France's main beet producing regions was 151 mm, still well below the 30-year average of 266 mm for the period.
